title: Shared prefix coalescing cache to reduce KV duplication across concurrent requests
creator: Maya Chen
description: We need a system-level cache that coalesces overlapping prompt prefixes across requests so that KV cache entries are deduplicated on-GPU. Aim is to reduce GPU memory pressure during peak throughput and improve effective batching by reusing existing KV slices rather than re-allocating or recomputing them for similar prefixes.
background: Current continuous batching treats each request's prefix KV separately; when many requests share common leading tokens (e.g., same system prompt or reused instruction templates) we end up with duplicated KV tensors in GPU memory and repeated attention computation. Previous attempts (ENG-9471, ENG-15820) explored fingerprinting and compact KV management but didn't address cross-request coalescing for partial overlaps and multi-tenant safety at runtime.
proposal:
Introduce a Shared Prefix Coalescing Cache (SPCC) with these components:
- Canonical token fingerprinting with collision-resistant hash and token-length encoding
- Chunked KV storage: split KV rows into fixed-size prefix shards to allow reuse when prefixes partially overlap
- Reference-counted GPU tensors with tenant-aware ACLs
- On-write deduplication: when a request computes KV for a prefix shard, check SPCC for existing shard; if found, attach reference instead of allocating new tensor
- Eviction policy tuned by LRU weighted by token length and request frequency, with background compaction to merge adjacent shards
- Integration points with continuous-batching router to prefer routes that enable shard reuse
- Optional compression for cold shards (4-bit quantized storage in host memory + on-demand dequantize)
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end system reduces peak GPU memory dedicated to KV by at least 20% on production traffic replay (95th percentile) without increasing median latency by >5%.
2) No cross-tenant data leakage: ACLs prevent attaching shard references across tenant boundaries unless configured for shared templates.
3) SPCC can accommodate partial prefix reuse: shards reused for >=50% overlap scenarios.
4) Eviction and refcount lifecycle produce no UVM allocations spikes during steady-state.
5) Benchmarks + dashboards (console/runtime-1.22) showing memory reduction and request latency per model.
tasks: Implement refcounted GPU tensor pool and allocator hooks
Modify KV write path to check & attach shards
Add ACL checks and tenant tagging
risks: Hash collisions producing incorrect reuse — mitigated with long hashes + length encoding
Increased CPU overhead for shard lookup under high QPS — mitigate with high-throughput hashmap (e.g., memkind or robin-hood) and sharding
Complexity in refcount lifecycle causing memory leaks — add audit tools and counters
Edge cases where reuse increases latency due to dequant/decompress on hot path — measure and provide config to disable for latency-critical models
